about: External datasets, outcome models and simulators linked to Text2WetLab tasks. Links and metadata only: nothing third-party is stored in this repo. `relation` is `direct` (from a task's own source paper) or `related` (same method, different study). The `verification` block is written by scripts/check_linked_resources.py.
found: Web search plus Zenodo, Hugging Face, PyPI, Crossref and GitHub API queries, 2026-10-13.

resources.name: T4 DNA ligase four-base overhang fidelity profile and NEBridge design tools
resources.what: Measured ligation frequency for all 256 four-base overhangs; drives tools that predict Golden Gate assembly fidelity for a chosen overhang set (Ligase Fidelity Viewer, GetSet, SplitSet).
resources.licence: ACS AuthorChoice (paper); data in the paper's supporting information
resources.notes: Location and format of the raw overhang table not checked; read the supporting information before using it in a grader.

verification.title: Comprehensive Profiling of Four Base Overhang Ligation Fidelity by T4 DNA Ligase and Application to DNA Assembly

resources.name: DNA Cauldron
resources.what: Cloning simulation: given parts and an enzyme, predicts the constructs a Golden Gate (or Gibson, BASIC, BioBrick) assembly yields and reports assembly flaws.
resources.notes: Candidate for outcome-aware grading: does the model's fragment and overhang choice assemble into the intended plasmid?

resources.name: pydna
resources.what: In-silico PCR (primers + template -> product), restriction digestion, ligation, Gibson and Golden Gate assembly.
resources.notes: Candidate check for colony PCR: do the primers amplify the intended product from the template?

resources.name: AssemblyTron v0.0.8 archive
resources.what: The archived release of the code behind the task's source paper. Software, not a results dataset.

resources.name: Sequence-specific PCR amplification efficiency prediction (1D CNN)
resources.what: Deep-learning model predicting amplification efficiency from sequence in multi-template PCR.
resources.notes: Code and training-data location not checked.

verification.title: Predicting sequence-specific amplification efficiency in multi-template PCR with deep learning

resources.name: PrimerCast
resources.what: Experimental dataset of primer-target PCR reactions with amplification-efficiency labels (reported as 50,760 reactions) and a predictive model (NeurIPS 2025).
resources.notes: Dataset size is from the conference abstract, not counted here.

resources.name: LiqTransferOptimizer
resources.what: Code and collected data for optimising liquid-handling parameters for viscous liquid transfers on pipetting robots (gravimetric transfer accuracy).
resources.notes: The closest public data on how accurately a robot delivers a commanded volume, which the Opentrons simulator does not model.

resources.name: Opentrons/PhysicalAI
resources.what: Opentrons' own robot dataset on Hugging Face (reported as Flex teleoperation episodes).
resources.notes: No licence stated on the dataset card. Contents not inspected.

resources.name: labos-sim/real_human_pipetting_lerobot_anonymized
resources.what: Multi-camera recordings of humans pipetting, with success/failure annotations (LeRobot format).
resources.notes: Real-world failure labels: relevant to physical faults a simulator cannot see.

resources.name: lerobotForScienceEdu/AgarBadge_v1_1st_Liquid-Handling_100_20251203
resources.what: Robot liquid-handling demonstrations in LeRobot format.

resources.name: AutoBio
resources.what: MuJoCo-based simulation and benchmark for robot manipulation in a biology lab (pipette aspiration, tube handling, centrifuge loading); task datasets on Hugging Face under autobio-bench.
resources.notes: Models robot manipulation, not the biology. arXiv 2505.14030.

resources.name: Pipette: embodied simulation platform and benchmark for wet-lab robotics
resources.what: Embodied simulation platform with 12 wet-lab tasks (sample handling, instrument interaction, lid operation, alignment).

resources.name: Source paper results: Evaluation of two automated low-cost RNA extraction protocols for SARS-CoV-2 detection
resources.what: Ct comparisons of the in-house OT-2 protocol against a commercial kit, reported in the paper.
resources.notes: Data-availability section and supporting files not opened. The task instruction gives this paper a different title; Crossref's is the one used here.

verification.title: Evaluation of two automated low-cost RNA extraction protocols for SARS-CoV-2 detection

resources.name: RNA extraction alternative method for SARS-CoV-2 molecular diagnosis
resources.what: Data from a different study evaluating an alternative RNA extraction method for SARS-CoV-2 diagnosis.
resources.notes: Not the task's protocol; useful only as outcome data for the same kind of experiment.

verification.title: RNA extraction alternative method for SARS-CoV-2 molecular diagnosis

resources.name: Comparison of two RNA extraction methods for the molecular detection of SARS-CoV-2 from nasopharyngeal swab samples
resources.what: Raw data of a study comparing two RNA extraction methods.
resources.notes: Not the task's protocol. The record exists but lists no public files (restricted or embargoed).

verification.title: Comparison of two RNA extraction methods for the molecular detection of SARS-CoV-2 from nasopharyngeal swab samples

gaps.finding: No outcome model and no public dataset of transformation efficiency found; only small experimental studies. The APEX paper reports its results in the text with no data deposit recorded.
No quantitative model or dataset for SPRI bead clean-up found; only vendor rules of thumb (bead ratio versus retained fragment size), which vary by bead lot.
The Slowpoke paper has no data deposit recorded; the PCR resources listed are for the method in general.
